meta.name: Save, search, and summarize Telegram links with Google Sheets and Supabase

options.systemMessage:
You are the Telegram front door of a second brain - the user's personal library of saved links.

Every incoming message is one of these cases - decide and act:
1. Contains a URL -> call save_link with the exact URL and the surrounding words as note. ALWAYS, even if the user adds commentary. If a message contains SEVERAL URLs, call save_link once per URL, then report all results together in one reply.
2. Asks a question -> pick the right search tool (rules below), then answer ONLY from its results.
3. Anything else (a statement with no URL) -> reply briefly with what you do: file links (share any URL, optionally with a comment that gets saved with it), answer questions about the library, and /clear resets the chat memory (never the library). Do not store anything.

Choosing between the two search tools:
- search_library (the spreadsheet): complete and always current. Use for listing items, filtering by category, counts, dates, URLs. It is the source of truth.
- search_content (Supabase vectors): semantic search over the full text of saved pages. Use for questions about what an article says, explains or discusses. When a fact conflicts with search_library, trust search_library.

After save_link: report back in 2-4 short markdown lines per saved link using the tool result - the action taken (created vs updated - mention when a duplicate was avoided), 📁 category, 🔖 **title**, and the summary. If the result says not_saved (the page could not be read), tell the user plainly: the page could not be read so NOTHING was saved - suggest sending the link again in a while, since sites often block automated readers only temporarily.

For questions: be short and direct, bold the key fact, include the URL when citing a card. If nothing matches, say the library has nothing on that topic yet.

Reply in the language the user writes in. If a tool call fails, say it plainly and ask the user to try again - never claim something was saved when it was not.

Never invent information that is not in tool results. Never skip save_link when a URL arrives - filing links is your primary job.

parameters.toolDescription: Read the COMPLETE list of saved links from the library spreadsheet - every card with all its fields (Category, Title, Summary, My Note, URL, Source, First Saved, Last Updated, Times Saved, ID). Always current - this is the source of truth. Use for listing links, filtering by category, counting, and questions about dates, URLs or the user's own notes. NOT for questions about what a page's full text says - use search_content for that.

parameters.text:
🧠 I save links!

Share any post or article - I read it, summarize it, categorize it, and file it. Add a comment next to the link and I keep that too.

Ask me anything about your saved links ("what was that article about agents?", "list my AI Tools links").

Send /clear to reset our chat memory - your saved links are never touched.

parameters.content:
## 🚪 The Brain Door - one agent, one library of links
The agent only ROUTES and TALKS. All filing logic lives in the deterministic Save Link path behind a webhook:
• save_link -> 🔗 Save Link (clean URL, read page, upsert on URL - never duplicates; your comment is kept in My Note)
• search_library -> reads the Sheet live (complete, current - lists, counts, categories)
• search_content -> semantic search over the full text of saved pages (RAG)

Memory is per chat, so follow-up questions work. Adding email/Slack/voice input later = another trigger feeding this same agent. Swapping Google Sheets for Notion = replace only the storage nodes inside the Save Link path.

parameters.content:
## 🔗 Save Link (tool)
Called by the Brain Door agent. Deterministic by design: clean the URL (dedup key) → read the page via r.jina.ai → look up this exact URL → AI writes a concrete title + summary and reuses existing categories → upsert matched on URL. Same link in = same row out, always. Returns a compact result the agent reports back.

If the page cannot be read (site blocks the reader), NOTHING is saved - the bot says so and asks you to retry later. No guess-cards in the library.

parameters.toolDescription: Save a link (URL) into the second brain library. It reads the page, summarizes it, categorizes it, and updates the existing card if this URL was saved before (never duplicates). Call this whenever the user message contains a URL. Returns what was filed.

Semantic search over the FULL TEXT of saved pages in the second brain. Use for questions about what an article/page actually says or discusses (concepts, explanations, details). Returns the most similar text chunks with metadata (id, url, title, category, saved_at). NOT for listing all items in a category, counting, or date filtering - use search_library for those.

parameters.content:
## 🛠️ One-time setup (run once)

**1 · Sheet**: click 'Run Setup Once' → Execute. Creates the 'Second Brain - Link Library' spreadsheet (tab: Links) with columns ID, URL, Title, Category, Summary, My Note, Source, First Saved, Last Updated, Times Saved - then deletes the temporary seed row.
⚠️ AFTER it runs: the 'Spreadsheet Id' node outputs the new sheet's ID → paste it into Document → By ID on `Find This Link` · `Read All Cards` · `Save to Library` · `search_library`.

**2 · Supabase**: create a free Supabase project and run the SQL from the note on the right in its SQL editor - it creates the `documents` table + `match_documents` function at **3072 dimensions**, sized for the Google Gemini embeddings this flow uses (switch to 1536 if you swap in OpenAI embeddings).

parameters.content:
## 🧠 Second Brain - Link Library (Telegram Agent)

Send any link to your Telegram bot - the agent reads the page with Jina Reader (r.jina.ai), writes a concrete summary, picks a category (reusing existing ones), and files it into Google Sheets. Send the same link again and it updates the existing card - never a duplicate. Ask questions and it answers from your library, including semantic (RAG) search over the full text of every saved page via Supabase vectors.

## Who's it for
Anyone who saves links every day and can never find them again - and n8n builders who want a clean AI Agent + tools + RAG pattern to extend.

## How it works
- A Telegram AI agent routes every message: URL → save, question → search, anything else → a short how-to reply. /clear resets the per-chat memory.
- save_link calls a deterministic webhook path: normalize the URL (the dedup key) → read the page via Jina Reader → an AI librarian writes title + concrete summary and reuses existing categories → upsert matched on URL. Your comment stays on the card (My Note). If a page cannot be read, nothing is filed - the bot tells you to retry instead of saving guesses.
- On every save, old vectors are deleted and the full page text is re-chunked and re-embedded into Supabase - a true replace, so RAG never serves stale versions.
- Two search tools: search_library (the Sheet - source of truth for lists, counts, categories) and search_content (semantic search over full page text).

## Requirements
- Telegram bot token
- Google Sheets
- AI chat model + Google Gemini embeddings (or your own)
- Supabase project (free tier is fine)
- Jina Reader (r.jina.ai) - free, no API key needed (better with API)

## How to set up
1. Create the credentials above and select them on each node. Create ONE Header Auth credential and use it in TWO places: the 'save link' webhook and the save_link agent tool (same header name + value).
2. Run the SQL from the Supabase note in your project's SQL editor.
3. Click 'Run Setup Once' → Execute: it creates the spreadsheet; the last node ('Spreadsheet Id') outputs its ID.
4. Paste that ID into Document → By ID on 4 nodes: Find This Link · Read All Cards · Save to Library · search_library.
5. In the save_link tool, change the URL to your instance: https://YOUR-DOMAIN/webhook/second-brain-save-link
6. Publish and send your bot a link 🎉

## How to customize
- Swap Google Sheets for Notion (or any wiki): storage is isolated inside the Save Link path - replace only those nodes; the agent and tools stay untouched.
- Add doorways: email, Slack or voice = another trigger feeding the same agent; each caller passes its own `source`.
- Tune the Librarian prompt (summary style, category rules), the model nodes (any OpenAI-compatible router), or RAG settings (chunk size, topK).

## 🗄️ Supabase setup - run this SQL once in your project's SQL editor
```
-- Reset (harmless if nothing exists yet)
drop function if exists match_documents;
drop table if exists documents;

-- Enable the pgvector extension to work with embedding vectors
create extension if not exists vector
with
  schema extensions;

-- Create a table to store your documents
create table documents (
  id bigserial primary key,
  content text, -- corresponds to Document.pageContent
  metadata jsonb, -- corresponds to Document.metadata
  embedding extensions.vector(3072) -- 1536 works for OpenAI embeddings, 3072 for Gemini change if needed
);

-- Create a function to search for documents
create function match_documents (
  query_embedding extensions.vector(3072),
  match_count int default null,
  filter jsonb DEFAULT '{}'
) returns table (
  id bigint,
  content text,
  metadata jsonb,
  similarity float
)
language plpgsql
as $$
#variable_conflict use_column
begin
  return query
  select
    id,
    content,
    metadata,
    1 - (documents.embedding <=> query_embedding) as similarity
  from documents
  where metadata @> filter
  order by documents.embedding <=> query_embedding
  limit match_count;
end;
$$;
```
